conviction_note: The baseline's 2.19% median is unusable - its own verdict is cadence_implausible because the six matched 6-Ks are monthly filings, and this name moved -24.6% pre-market on a single tariff 6-K in April and +7.4% pre-market on the last quarterly release - so I anchor magnitude on the 44.7% realised vol instead; I take a moderate positive because BRP's FY27 guidance has been suspended since 2026-04-15 and this print is the natural venue to reinstate it, with the last quarter and the most recent broker comment both pointing at successful mitigation.

findings.finding: BRP has been operating without fiscal-2027 guidance since 2026-04-15, when it suspended the outlook after the Section 232 amendment replaced a 50% metal-content tariff with a 25% tariff on the total value of imported snowmobiles and most off-road vehicles, and quantified the potential incremental cost at 'in excess of $500M for the remainder of the year, before any mitigation measures' - so this print is the first fiscal-second-quarter release in which management must either reinstate a guide or explain why it still cannot.
findings.why_not_priced: A withdrawn guide means there is no consensus anchor to beat or miss, so the print is a genuine information release rather than a comparison exercise - and the baseline the market would use for magnitude (a 2.19% median from monthly operational 6-Ks) is wrong by an order of magnitude. Note what the tape says: the stock is only 22.5% below its 52-week high and has recovered most of the April gap, i.e. the market has quietly assumed the $500M is largely mitigable without the company having confirmed it. There is no news-search coverage of this ticker at all (n_queries=0 in every admissible sweep), so no preview tests that assumption.
findings.independence: The same document records the company's own first data point on mitigation from a separate release six weeks later - the 2026-05-28 quarter beat with a 'stronger outlook despite tariff pressures' and the stock up 7.4% pre-market - https://ooc.bz/l/103877

findings.finding: The only sell-side action in the capture during the run-in is positive and recent: TD Securities made favourable comments on DOO on 2026-08-18, logged as the day's sole positive broker comment, and it followed a 2026-04-15 downgrade to Hold from Buy at TD Cowen - so the direction of sell-side revision has turned while the stock is still 22.5% off its high.
findings.why_not_priced: The item is a one-line trading-desk recap with no substance attached and no target or rating given, so it moved nothing; it is useful only as the sign of the most recent professional revision into a print with no guide. Weak on its own, which is why it is a fraction of finding 1.
findings.independence: none - same captured document as finding 1, so this is one source cluster and the scorer should collapse it.

searched_and_found_nothing: any 6-K between 2026-05-28 and the print - a fourteen-week filing gap, so no tariff update, no mitigation announcement and no pre-release from the company
any equity or debt issuance in 2026 (the SUPPL/FWP notes offering is from December 2025)
any 13D or activist filing; only passive 13G/As, the most recent 2026-05-15
any Form 4 or insider filing at all - as a Canadian issuer BRP's insider trades are on SEDI, not EDGAR, so this channel is simply unavailable
any news-wire coverage, consensus estimate or dealer-inventory/retail-registration channel data: n_queries=0 in every admissible sweep
any confirmation of whether Section 232 tariffs on imported ORVs and snowmobiles have changed again since 6 April 2026
baseline_tension: It agrees with the five-day run-in (+5.1%) and with 4 of 6 tagged reactions being positive, but it argues the baseline's 2.19% magnitude is far too small - this is primarily a magnitude finding, and the direction is the weaker half of it.
